preventiveCare.title: Preventive Care
preventiveCare.pageDescription: Proactive tips to keep your crops healthy and thriving.

properspacing.title: Proper Spacing
properspacing.description: Plant tomato seedlings at least 24-36 inches apart to ensure good air circulation, which helps prevent fungal diseases like blight.

consistentwatering.title: Consistent Watering
consistentwatering.description: Water deeply and at the base of the plant to avoid wetting the foliage. Inconsistent watering can lead to blossom-end rot.

mulching.title: Mulching
mulching.description: Apply a layer of organic mulch (like straw or wood chips) to conserve moisture, suppress weeds, and prevent soil-borne diseases from splashing onto leaves.

croprotation.title: Crop Rotation
croprotation.description: Avoid planting leafy greens in the same spot year after year to prevent the buildup of soil pests and diseases.

shadeinhotweather.title: Shade in Hot Weather
shadeinhotweather.description: Provide partial shade during the hottest parts of the day to prevent bolting (premature flowering) and scorched leaves.

monitorforpests.title: Monitor for Pests
monitorforpests.description: Regularly check for aphids and cabbage worms. Hand-pick larger pests or use insecticidal soap for smaller ones.

supportandstaking.title: Support and Staking
supportandstaking.description: Provide stakes or cages to support the plants as they grow heavy with fruit. This keeps fruit off the ground and improves air circulation.

fertilizeappropriately.title: Fertilize Appropriately
fertilizeappropriately.description: Use a balanced, low-nitrogen fertilizer. Too much nitrogen can encourage lush foliage at the expense of fruit production.

watchforbacterialspot.title: Watch for Bacterial Spot
watchforbacterialspot.description: Avoid working with plants when they are wet to prevent the spread of bacterial diseases. Use copper-based sprays as a preventive measure if needed.

addNewLog.title: Add New Log
addNewLog.description: Record a new activity for your field.
